subject: MSA + Order Form: initial draft, signing authority & export-control asks

Subject: Draft MSA + Order Form for review

Hi Laura —

Thanks for the quick intro last week. Attached are the initial drafts (Acme_MSA_Draft_v1.docx, OrderForm_Acme.xlsx). A few items we want to surface up front so your team can scope legal/security asks: 

- Signing authority: our legal team is asking for confirmation of who signs for Redwood on the MSA vs the Order Form. Could you provide the typical signatory setup and any threshold values that require higher-level approval?
- Export controls: Acme does sensitive analytics for a handful of overseas subsidiaries (APAC/EU). We need to confirm whether Redwood has any restrictions or specific export-control language to include.
- SOC 2 evidence: send your SOC 2 report or where we can download it (or an NDA gateway if needed).
- Sandbox / pre-prod access: timeline to get a sandbox invite for our engineers (SFTP/API keys) so we can validate integration during contracting.

Target go-live: Oct 1, 2025 — we realize that's tight, but we wanted to flag the date. Can your team confirm availability for a kickoff call early next week?

Attachments: Acme_MSA_Draft_v1.docx (docx), OrderForm_Acme.xlsx (xlsx)

Thanks,
Chris Perez

Acme Analytics

Subject: Re: Draft MSA + Order Form for review

Hi Chris —

Thanks for sending these over and for the timeline. We're happy to kick off review and support the sandbox onboarding. A few quick answers and asks from our side: 

1) Signing authority: Our standard is that the CEO or Head of GTM signs MSAs above $500k ARR; below that the VP of Finance or General Counsel can sign. For Order Forms we typically use an authorized signatory at VP level. I'll confirm the current signer names and whether we can pre-approve by exception for this deal.

2) Export controls: this is more nuanced. Kim (cc'd) owns legal intake and will triage export-control language with Security. Can you flag which subsidiaries / jurisdictions are in scope and whether data will be hosted in EU/APAC regions?

3) SOC 2 evidence: we have a link behind an NDA portal; Kimberly, can you share the download link or an interim summary? If Acme needs the full report we can open a comms channel for redaction/secure transfer.

4) Sandbox access: Karthik, can we provision a developer sandbox for Acme's test team? Chris, send the list of engineers + desired IP ranges.

Proposed next steps:
- I'll run a quick signatory check this afternoon and update you.
- Kimberly will kick off redline triage and share a redline plan.
- Karthik will confirm sandbox provisioning ETA (usually 48-72 hours after we receive access details).

Suggest a 30-min kickoff Monday (Aug 18) — are you available?

Best,
Laura Bennett
Contract Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com

Date: Sat, 17 Aug 2025 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft MSA + Order Form for review — redline plan and evidence path

Laura / team —

Thanks, Laura. I reviewed the draft MSA and Order Form at a high level. I’ll run a formal redline sprint but here’s the immediate plan and blockers I see: 

- Priority triage: Security/data residency / export-control clauses, liability caps, IP carve-outs, and billing cadence.
- Export control: Need the list of territories and whether Acme will transmit controlled data (e.g., export-controlled source datasets). If so, we'll need our Security & Compliance to do a jurisdictional review and add targeted language or carveouts.
- SOC 2: We will provide a secure link to the SOC 2 report. I will request a temporary NDA-protected download (typical turnaround 24 hours).
- Signatory matrix: Please provide the completed Counterparty_Signer_List.csv with names, titles, and signature authority thresholds. That will speed approvals.

Attachments: Redline_Plan_Outline.pdf (pdf stub) — contains proposed triage, owners, and a 5-business-day redline cadence.

For the timeline: if we start the redline sprint on Monday (18th) and Acme is responsive to clarifying Qs, we can aim to have a clean MSA and Order Form for approval by Aug 25. That lets us hit a mid-September production target but not Oct 1 comfortably — the earlier sandbox access (for QA) will help.

Karthik — can your team confirm the engineer list and desired sandbox IP ranges?

Chris / Natalie — please reply with the signer list and the export-control jurisdictions. If you prefer, we can take these items offline via a short form we provide.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Security Intake
Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com

Laura / Kimberly / Karthik —

Appreciate the fast turnaround. Attached is the Counterparty_Signer_List.csv with signers and thresholds. Quick answers below: 

- Export-control jurisdictions: APAC (Singapore, Hong Kong), EU (Germany), plus our US operations. Data hosting will be in the US by default; we plan to replicate to EU for compliance with one EU subsidiary — no controlled datasets will be exported to non-US entities except for aggregated analytics outputs.
- SOC 2: we can accept the NDA-protected link; please send the link and any instructions.
- Sandbox: our integration team list is attached in the CSV (engineer emails + IP ranges). We request SFTP keys and a temporary API key for testing.

DocuSign/Procurement: we've created a DocuSign envelope to track signatures — link below. HubSpot deal link also provided for reference.
